1.title: T&I Committee Republicans
1.description:
The Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure has jurisdiction over the nation's highways, bridges, railroads, transit and aviation systems, and maritime and waterborne transportation.  

The Committee also oversees programs for clean water infrastructure, pipeline safety, economic development, disaster preparedness and response, and the transportation of hazardous materials. 

These are issues that serve as the foundation of our economy and our way of life.  Committee Republicans are working to strengthen that foundation to ensure the safe, efficient transportation of people and goods, and provide the necessary infrastructure for our communities across the nation.

Graves also said that if Biden chooses to raise taxes to pay for the final infrastructure package, he will have trouble gaining Republican support.

756.title: Press Conference: Unveiling of WRRDA (The Water Resources Reform & Development Act 2013)
756.description:
The leaders of the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Subcommittee on Water Resources and Environment introduced the Water Resources Reform and Development Act of 2013 (WRRDA) during a Wednesday press conference in the U.S. Capitol.

Through this type of water resources legislation, Congress authorizes the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to carry out its missions to develop, maintain, and support our Nation's vital port and waterways infrastructure needs, and support effective and targeted flood protection and environmental restoration needs.  Historically, Congress has passed such legislation every two years to provide clear direction to the Administration and the Corps, but no bill has been signed into law since 2007.  The Water Resources Reform and Development Act will be one of the most policy and reform focused measures of its kind in the last two decades.

One of the Committee's top priorities this Congress, WRDA legislation will focus on developing, maintaining, and supporting the Nation's port and waterway infrastructure, as well as addressing targeted flood protection and environmental restoration needs.

784.title: Petri on MAP-21 Implementation
784.description:
Subcommittee on Highways and Transit Chairman Tom Petri (R-WI) opens a March 14, 2013 hearing focused on ensuring the Administration is implementing reforms to help streamline the surface transportation project approval process, consolidate Department of Transportation programs, improve program accountability, and other improvements included in the Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century Act (MAP-21).  

MAP-21, signed into on July 6, 2012, authorizes the federal highway, transit and highway safety programs through September 30, 2014.

"MAP-21 consolidated or eliminated over 70 federal programs that were duplicative," said ,

792.title: FAA Can't Justify 90-Minute Delays Under Sequester
792.description: At a February 27, 2013 Congressional hearing, the head of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) could not provide information to support repeated claims from the Obama Administration that the nation may expect 90-minute flight delays due to sequester spending reductions.  When asked about data to support this claim by Mark Meadows (R-NC), FAA Administrator Michael Huerta responded, "I can't tell you with precision that it would be 90 minutes every day."

797.title: Shuster on Sandy Recovery Improvement Act
797.description: Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Chairman Bill Shuster (R-PA) discusses the Sandy Recovery Improvement Act (H.R. 219), a bipartisan bill he introduced with Rep. Jeff Denhma (R-CA) and other Committee leaders to speed up and streamline federal disaster recovery programs.  The measure specifically targets improvements to help strengthen the Hurricane Sandy recovery process and reduce costs as communities rebound from the recent superstorm and other future disasters.

804.title: Chairman Mica Discusses Hearing in Empty Federal Building on News4
804.description:
Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Chairman John L. Mica (R-FL) and Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee Chairman Jeff Denham (R-CA) led a Congressional hearing on June 19 at the vacant Georgetown Heating Plant, a high-value federal asset which hasn't operated for over a decade but has cost the taxpayers $3.5 million in operating expenses.

News 4 discusses the problem of vacant federal buildings across the country, as well as in our Nation's Capital.

808.description:
Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Chairman John L. Mica (R-FL) appeared on FOX and Friends on June 4, 2012 to discuss another TSA meltdown at an airport in Florida which may involve a substantial number of TSA employees, including high-ranking airport security officials.

This reported failure comes on the heels of other security operations meltdowns at airports in New York, Newark, Palm Beach, Honolulu, Charlotte, and Los Angeles.

815.title: Chairman Mica Appears on Stossel to Discuss Vacant and Underutilized Federal Buildings
815.description:
On May 10, 2012 Chairman Mica appeared on FOX Business with John Stossel to discuss the poor management and underutilization of federal properties around the country.  They toured the Old Post Office in Washington, D.C., which has been sitting partially vacant for a decade, costing taxpayers $6.5 million every year.
They also toured the Cotton Annex, a 89,000 square-foot building occupying a large parcel of highly desirable but underdeveloped land one block away from the National Mall.  The building has been empty for years, but GSA has no plans to put this asset, conservatively valued at $150 million, to use in a way that benefits the taxpayers.

828.title: Chairman Mica Discusses TSA on Stossel
828.description:
Chairman Mica appeared on FOX Business on April 6th to discuss the mismanagement of the Transportation Security Administration (TSA). Mica highlighted the need for dramatic reform of the TSA. 

The list of TSA operational failures has grown over the last ten years, and the agency has expended a significant amount of taxpayer resources in too many efforts that have provided little or no security benefits.

832.title: Chairman Mica's interview with CBS on Cruise Ship Safety
832.description: A Congressional hearing on Wednesday, February 29, reviewed the safety of cruise vessels operating out of U.S. ports and lessons learned in light of the recent COSTA CONCORDIA accident off the coast of Italy. On February 27, a fire occurred onboard another cruise ship operated by the same company; this vessel is currently adrift in the Indian Ocean. Witnesses on Wednesday included survivors of the COSTA CONCORDIA accident.

839.description:
On February 2, 2012, the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee approved landmark jobs legislation to reauthorize and reform federal surface transportation programs and rebuild the nation's roads, bridges and infrastructure.

On Wednesday, the Committee began consideration of the American Energy & Infrastructure Jobs Act, a bill introduced in the House by Transportation Committee Chairman John L. Mica (R-FL) and Highways and Transit Subcommittee Chairman John J. Duncan, Jr. (R-TN). The legislation was early the next morning.

864.title: Chairman Mica's Opening Remarks at Oct. 5 NextGen Hearing
864.description:
Federal auditors, including the Inspector General of the Department of Transportation (DOT) and the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO), testified before Congress on Wednesday, October 5 to point to problems and rising costs in the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) critical NextGen air traffic control modernization effort.

FAA's poor management continues to delay NextGen progress, and the agency has failed to develop adequate benchmarks and a long-term plan for implementing the multi-billion dollar project to transition the nation's air traffic control system from ground-based radar and antiquated 1950s technology to a modern satellite-based system.

865.title: Rep. Petri at NextGen Hearing
865.description:
A Congressional hearing on Wednesday, October 5 examined the costs, benefits, progress and management of the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) NextGen air traffic control modernization program.

Wednesday's hearing, chaired by U.S. Rep. Tom Petri (R-WI), focused on the FAA's progress in delivering measureable benefits to aviation users, as well as the agency's projections for future benefits to be gained from federal and industry investment. The FAA has promised efficiency gains through NextGen by optimizing air traffic controller performance, consolidating obsolete facilities, enhanced safety improvements, and improved operational efficiency of the national airspace system. For example, the FAA estimates that with NextGen aviation users will save 1.4 billion gallons of fuel and see a 14 million ton reduction in carbon emissions through 2018. However, the airspace users who will be asked to invest in expensive NextGen compatible avionics must have confidence in FAA's ability to manage the program and deliver the benefits.

866.title: Rep. LoBiondo at Coast Guard Acquisitions Program Hearing
866.description:
The Subcommittee on Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation, chaired by U.S. Rep. Frank A. LoBiondo (R-NJ), held a hearing on Tuesday, October 4 to examine the Coast Guard Acquisition Program and the related challenges that have faced the Service since it took control of modernizing its aging fleet of assets in 2007.

The Coast Guard Acquisition Program has been experiencing significant cost overruns and setbacks that were the subject of a recent GAO report entitled "Action Needed as Approved Deepwater Program Remains Unachievable." The report found that it will be impossible for the Coast Guard to complete its major acquisitions without breaching its 2007 baseline of 20 to 25 years for construction and delivery at a total cost of $24.2 billion. The GAO estimates it could take an additional 10 years to complete and could cost at least an additional $5 billion.

867.title: Rep. Gibbs' Opening Statement at Inland Waterways Hearing
867.description:
A Congressional hearing on Wednesday, September 21 focused on the importance of the nation's system of inland waterways, and the challenges in maintaining this aging but economically important transportation system.

The U.S. Inland Waterways Transportation System is the nation's most cost-effective and energy efficient means for transporting commercial goods, especially major bulk commodities like grain, coal, and petroleum products. This transportation system is also a key component of state and local economies and job creation efforts and is essential in maintaining economic competitiveness and national security.

873.title: Chairman Mica on EU Plan to Tax U.S. Air Carriers
873.description:
A Congressional hearing on Wednesday, July 27 examined the European Union's (EU) plan to tax U.S. air carriers and other operators under the EU's Emissions Trading Scheme. 

The hearing focused on the EU's actions in the context of international law, and the impact of the EU's Emissions Trading Scheme on U.S. operators, the competitiveness of the U.S. aviation industry, and U.S. aviation jobs.

Beginning on January 1, 2012, all air carriers flying into or out of an EU airport will be forced to participate in the EU's Emissions Trading Scheme, despite objections by the United States and other governments. U.S. airlines have also challenged the policy before the European Court of Justice as a violation of international law.

881.title: Gibbs on the Realize America's Maritime Promise Act
881.description:
The Water Resources and Environment Subcommittee, chaired by U.S. Rep. Bob Gibbs (R-OH), held a legislative hearing today to examine H.R. 104, the Realize America's Maritime Promise (RAMP) Act.

The RAMP Act, introduced by U.S. Rep. Charles Boustany (R-LA), requires that revenue coming into the Harbor Maintenance Trust Fund (HMTF) each year, including interest on the balance, is all invested in U.S. harbor construction and maintenance.

882.title: Rep. Denham's Opening Statement at July 6 Hearing on SEC Leasing Authority
882.description: Representative Jeff Denham, Chairman of the Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee, questioned the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Chairman and Inspector General regarding the Agency's recent lease of hundreds of thousands of square feet of unneeded space. As a result of Chairman Denham's investigation, the SEC agreed to give up its leasing authority and many of the SEC employees may also face prosecution from the Justice Department for backdating documents that "justified" the lease.

885.title: Fox Honolulu Discusses Mica's Call for Investigation of TSA Screening Meltdown
885.description:
Reports indicate that dozens of federal transportation security officers are to be fired after an alleged dramatic failure in security performance at Honolulu Airport.

U.S. Rep. John L. Mica (R-FL), Chairman of the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, and U.S. Rep. Jason Chaffetz (R-UT), Chairman of the National Security, Homeland Defense and Foreign Operations Subcommittee, wrote to the Department of Homeland Security Acting Inspector General to request the investigation of TSA security failures.

888.description:

Frank LoBiondo (R-NJ) held a hearing on Tuesday, June 14 to review the state of the Marine Transportation System (MTS) and explore ways to enhance the MTS to create jobs, improve the flow of commerce, and increase U.S. exports.

The hearing, entitled "Creating Jobs and Increasing U.S. exports by Enhancing the Marine Transportation System," examined the ways in which the MTS can be improved to meet the current challenges it faces.

889.title: Rep. John J. Duncan, Jr. at a June 13, 2011 Bus Safety Hearing
889.description:
Although travel by bus or motorcoach is one of the safest forms of transportation in the United States, recent high profile bus accidents in Virginia, New York, and New Jersey have raised concerns about safety and "rogue" bus operators who intentionally attempt to circumvent motorcoach safety regulations and continue to operate.
A Monday, June 13, 2011 hearing of the Full Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, chaired by U.S. Rep. John L. Mica (R-FL), examined federal safety programs and how best to improve bus safety.

893.title: Rep. Bill Shuster's Opening Statement at May 26 High-Speed Rail Hearing
893.description:
House Transportation Committee leaders outlined a dramatic change in direction to develop true high-speed passenger rail service in the Northeast Corridor (NEC) at a May 26 Full Committee hearing. Their proposal would transfer development of the nation's most congested corridor from Amtrak to private sector competition.

Committee Chairman John L. Mica (R-FL) and Rail Subcommittee Chairman Bill Shuster (R-PA) announced at the hearing that they are preparing legislation to significantly speed up development of high-speed rail and reduce high taxpayer subsidization of the project.

895.title: Rep. Petri's Floor Statement on Short-Term FAA Extension
895.description: H.R. 1893, the Airport and Airway Extension Act of 2011, Part II passed on the House floor on Monday, May 23, 2011.  It is a clean, short-term extension of the FAA funding and programs through June 30, 2011, ensuring that the FAA is able to continue operating until negotiations for a long-term FAA reauthorization are complete.

896.title: U.S. Rep. Jeff Denham's Opening Statement at May 12 Subcommittee Hearing
896.description:
The Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee, chaired by Denham, held a hearing to examine the bill he introduced, the Civilian Property Realignment Act (H.R. 1734), as well as a similar proposal by the Administration.

Members of Congress and witnesses representing the Administration and the private sector supported a proposal by U.S. Rep. Jeff Denham (R-CA) to employ a BRAC-like process to civilian properties in order to reduce the federal footprint and save taxpayers billions of dollars.

903.title: Chairman Mica Discusses Air Traffic Controllers Sleeping on the Job
903.description:
U.S. Rep. John L. Mica (R-FL), Chairman of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, released the following statement after an announcement by the U.S. Department of Transportation and the Federal Aviation Administration to double staffing levels during the midnight shift at air traffic control towers:

"Only in the federal government would you double up on workers, averaging $161,000 per year in salary and benefits, that aren't doing their job."

"This increase in staffing, when there is little to no traffic, also misdirects our resources and focus away from congested air traffic control facilities."

908.title: Rep. Shuster's Opening Statement at April 12 Railroads Subcommittee Hearing
908.description:
The Subcommittee on Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials, chaired by U.S. Rep. Bill Shuster (R-PA), conducted a hearing on Tuesday, April 12 to discuss reauthorization of federal hazardous materials transportation safety programs, as well as reforms to ensure safe, efficient hazmat transport and the reduction of regulatory burdens.

Some issues that were addressed at Tuesday's hearing were duplicative regulations and procedures, the issuance of special permits and approvals, the regulation of wetlines, and the opening of labeled and unlabeled packages.

910.title: Chairman Denham's Opening Statement from Subcommittee Hearing on Consolidating Federal Buildings
910.description:
A Congressional hearing on Wednesday, March 6 explored the potential for establishing a process, based on the military's Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) Commission, for consolidating federal office space and improving real estate management to save taxpayers billions of dollars.
A civilian BRAC process, which would establish a fair process of evaluating federal space needs, has the potential to save the taxpayers billions of dollars by addressing the currently underutilized federal real property and over-reliance on costly leasing.

925.title: Mica on TSA 'Cooking the Books'
925.description: The Screening Partnership Program was established in the Aviation Transportation Security Act (ATSA) after September 11, 2001, to enable airport authorities to "opt-out" of all-federal screening and instead use private screening contractors under federal standards, supervision and oversight.  Previously, TSA has misleadingly claimed that the cost of the privatized screening program is at least 17 percent higher than the cost of using screeners who are TSA employees.

950.title: Mica on Obama Tax & Spend Proposal
950.description: Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Ranking Member John Mica (R-FL) on FOX and Friends (Sept. 16, 2010) to discuss President Obama's latest tax and spend, so-called stimulus effort which throws more money at our economic problems without addressing the problems with the first stimulus.  Much of the infrastructure funding in the first stimulus still has not been spent, and Mica supports cutting red tape for projects and getting the existing authorized funding out the door more quickly.

963.title: Diaz-Balart on GSA Waste
963.description: Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Ranking Member Mario Diaz-Balart (R-FL) statement from a June 17, 2010 hearing on the General Services Administration's (GSA) fiscal year 2011 Capital Improvement and Leasing Program.  Diaz-Balart highlighted the waste of taxpayer dollars represented by the Administration's proposal for funding federal construction and leasing projects for 2011. One proposed project would renovate an over-built and over-budget courthouse that currently allows 1,500 square feet of building space for each employee -- more space than many families occupy.

970.title: Brian Rainville Testifies on Wasteful Stimulus
970.description: Brian Rainville, a teacher whose family farm is in Morses Line, Vermont, testifies that the federal government is planning to take a part of the farm and use millions in stimulus funds to rebuild a small border station at the Canadian border. 972.title: Diaz-Balart on Waste in Courthouse Program
972.description:
U.S. Rep. Mario Diaz-Balart (R-FL), Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee Ranking Member, calls the more than $800 million in tax dollars wasted on unnecessary courthouse construction an appalling example of government waste and mismanagement.

A Subcommittee hearing received testimony from the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO), which is working to finalize a report on the multibillion-dollar courthouse construction initiative of the federal judiciary and the General Services Administration (GSA).

Republicans applauded the progress made by the ports in dramatically cutting air pollution from trucks operating at their ports, and cautioned that efforts to reregulate the trucking industry and threaten small businesses are unnecessary for the success of clean truck programs.

974.title: Diaz-Balart on Economic Development Commissions
974.description:
At a Congressional hearing on the proposed fiscal year 2011 budgets for regional economic development commissions, Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee Ranking Member Mario Diaz-Balart (R-FL) stressed the importance of effectively leveraging commission funding and ensuring that job creation is a priority for distressed areas of the country.

Included among these commissions are the Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC), the Denali Commission, the Delta Regional Authority (DRA), the Northern Great Plains Regional Authority, the Southeast Crescent Regional Commission, the Southwest Border Regional Commission, and the Northern Border Regional Commission.

Such a limit of batteries used in devices ranging from cell phones to iPods to many medical devices may result in jobs and technological innovations moving outside of the United States.

1065.description: Rep. John L. Mica (R-FL), the Republican Leader on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, at a press conference with other Republican Congressional leaders on the Democrats' cap-and-trade legislation.  The Democratic Chairmen of nearly every House committee the bill has been referred to have allowed the bill through their committees without so much as a public hearing or legislative markup session.  The bill will kill jobs and significantly increase energy prices.

1070.title: Diaz-Balart on FEMA Disaster Housing
1070.description:
U.S. Rep. Mario Diaz-Balart (R-FL) statement from Congressional hearing on the ongoing housing issues that remain following Hurricane Katrina, which struck the Gulf Coast nearly four years ago.  5,000 individuals and households continue to live in the temporary housing provided them by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). 

Diaz-Balart is the Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee Ranking Member.  Statements and testimony from the hearing can be found at http://republicans.transportation.house.gov/hearings/hearingdetail.aspx?NewsID=605.

331.title: Take Five with T&I featuring Vice Ranking Member Valerie Foushee
331.description:
Vice Ranking Member Valerie Foushee knows that while 3.4 million miles of America's pipelines often go unnoticed, they’re essential to everyday life.

In Take Five with T&I, she shares with Rep. Rick Larsen how the PIPES Act of 2023 will make our pipelines safer and more efficient.

357.title: Clean Water Act of 2023 - Press Conference
357.description: Ranking Member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure Rick Larsen (D-WA), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Water Resources and Environment Grace Napolitano (D-CA), Rep. Don Beyer, Rep. Melanie Stansbury and over a hundred House Democrats will introduce the Clean Water Act of 2023. This legislation undoes the damage from the Supreme Court Sackett decision by reinstating the historic and bipartisan, federal-state partnership that has protected our rivers, streams, and wetlands for over 50 years; establishing a clear, level playing field for businesses and industries to thrive while protecting our precious natural resources; and ensuring clean water for our families and future generations.

622.title: "The Evolving Cybersecurity Landscape: Federal Perspectives on Securing the Nation's Infrastructure"
622.description:
Cyberattacks are a serious and evolving risk that affect transportation and infrastructure matters across T&I’s jurisdiction. Cyberattacks can result in tremendous financial damage, destruction of infrastructure assets, and even death. They impact governments, businesses, and individuals alike and have been growing in number and sophistication.
 
This hearing is the second of two full committee hearings on cybersecurity of the nation’s infrastructure. The first hearing was held in November 2021 and featured testimony from industry stakeholders and cybersecurity experts.

680.title: Infrastructure Is Calling and America is Ready to Answer with the INVEST in America Act
680.description: Infrastructure is calling and the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure is answering the call. Investing in our infrastructure—and investing in communities across the country—can create millions of good-paying jobs in underserved areas and lay the groundwork for not only a full economic recovery from the pandemic, but also usher in a new era of American innovation and prosperity. Join the committee, working people, unions, mayors, and communities from across the country who are united in building our country back better than ever through transformational infrastructure investment.

Investing in our infrastructure—and investing in communities across the country—can create millions of good-paying jobs in underserved areas and lay the groundwork for not only a full economic recovery from the pandemic, but also usher in a new era of American innovation and prosperity. Join the committee and mayors from across the country who are united in building our communities back better than ever through transformational infrastructure investment.
